text: Indeed, the argument from Vowles sounds flawed. Their disadvantage (of not having proper basic systems in place) exists regardless of a cost cap. The cost cap likely forces them to divert resources from the car and towards those systems, and if they should have the resources for both, this restriction must be frustrating in the short term. But once they are up to speed, it is the very cost cap that will ensure level playing field and a realistic chance at success. The price is, optimistically, a few lean years before they are truly in the running.
